lesson.summary: Cloud computing means getting IT resources on demand over the internet and paying only for what you use. Compared with buying your own servers and data centers, it trades large upfront costs for variable costs, lets you scale to real demand, and lets you launch in new places in minutes.
keyPoints: Cloud computing is on-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
Trade fixed expense for variable expense: pay for the capacity you use instead of buying servers upfront
Benefit from economies of scale: AWS combines usage from many customers, which lowers pay-as-you-go prices
Stop guessing capacity: scale resources up or down in minutes instead of over-buying or running short
Increase speed and agility: new IT resources are available in minutes instead of weeks
Stop spending money on running and maintaining data centers so you can focus on your own customers
Go global in minutes: deploy an application in several AWS Regions with a few clicks

scenarios.text: A small online shop expects a large spike in orders during a seasonal sale, but nobody knows how many visitors to expect. The owner does not want to buy servers that sit idle for the rest of the year.

questions.prompt: Which statement best defines cloud computing?

options.text: Buying your own servers and keeping them in an office server room
On-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
One large computer that a single company owns and shares only with its own staff
Software that is installed separately on each employee's laptop

questions.explanation: Cloud computing is on-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing. Owning servers in an office room is the traditional model it replaces. A single large computer used only by one company is not a cloud model by definition. Software installed on each laptop is the opposite of resources delivered on demand.

questions.statement: In the AWS Cloud you must buy the hardware before you can use any computing resources.
questions.explanation: False. The cloud removes the need to invest heavily in data centers and servers before you know how you will use them. You pay for the resources you consume.

questions.prompt: Which benefit of cloud computing matters most to the shop owner in this scenario?

options.text: Physical security of the data center
A fixed hardware cost that never changes

questions.explanation: Stop guessing capacity means you can access as much or as little capacity as you need and scale up or down quickly, so the shop does not pay for idle servers after the sale. Economies of scale lower prices but do not solve the capacity question. Physical security is an AWS responsibility, not the benefit in question. A fixed hardware cost is the problem the cloud removes.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements describe trading fixed expense for variable expense? (Choose two.)

options.text: You pay upfront for servers you may never use
You pay only for the resources you consume
Your costs can rise and fall with actual usage
You must sign a multi-year contract for all of your hardware

questions.explanation: Variable expense means you pay for what you consume, so costs go up and down with usage. Paying upfront for unused servers is the fixed-expense model. A multi-year hardware contract is also a fixed commitment.

questions.prompt: Match each cloud benefit with the example that shows it.

pairs.right: Adding more capacity within minutes when a campaign starts
A new test environment is ready in minutes instead of weeks
Deploying the same application in several Regions with a few clicks
Lower pay-as-you-go prices as AWS usage grows across many customers

questions.explanation: Each benefit maps to one example: scaling with demand shows stop guessing capacity, self-service provisioning in minutes shows speed and agility, multi-Region deployment shows going global, and lower prices from aggregated usage show economies of scale.

questions.prompt: Type the name of the pricing model in which you pay only for the resources you use.
questions.explanation: Pay-as-you-go pricing means you pay only for the resources you consume. It is the same idea as variable expense, which replaces fixed upfront costs.
